classification.difficultyReason: Read the figures as three-quarter and one-twelfth circles, equate their areas using radii r and r+6, and solve the resulting squared relationship using the taught trial or algebraic method.

content.prompt: The shapes in the diagram below have equal areas. Determine the value of $r$.

spec.description: Unshaded circle with its lower-right quadrant removed. Bounding radii point right and down, have matching single ticks, and enclose a right-angle square in the missing quadrant. The downward radius is labelled r.
spec.mathematics: The retained major sector has angle 270 degrees and radius r, so its area is three quarters of pi r squared.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question givens only; no supplied solution is drawn.

spec.description: Unshaded 30-degree minor sector with a horizontal lower radius and an upper radius sloping right. Both radii carry matching double ticks. The lower radius is labelled r + 6.
spec.mathematics: The minor sector has angle 30 degrees and radius r + 6, so its area is one twelfth of pi times (r + 6) squared. Drawing coordinates are construction values, not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question givens only; no supplied solution is drawn.

answer.worked:
The left shape is $\frac34$ of a circle; the right shape is $\frac{30}{360}=\frac1{12}$ of a circle.

$$\begin{align*}
\frac34\pi r^2&=\frac1{12}\pi(r+6)^2\\
\frac34 r^2&=\frac1{12}(r+6)^2\\
\frac{r^2}{(r+6)^2}&=\frac19
\end{align*}$$

By trial and error, $r=3$. Checking:

$$\begin{align*}
\frac{3^2}{(3+6)^2}&=\frac9{81}\\
\frac9{81}&=\frac19
\end{align*}$$

Alternate method using quadratic equations:

$$\begin{align*}
\frac34 r^2&=\frac1{12}(r^2+12r+36)\\
-2r^2+3r+9&=0\\
(-2r-3)(r-3)&=0
\end{align*}$$

$r=3$ or $r=-\frac32$, but a radius must be positive. Therefore $r=3$.
